reason: The PROBLEM is real and the seat's numbers are exact — I drove lately.html in Chromium at 1440/1280/768/390, both grounds, states full/partial/quiet/loading, and measured .bar-val vs the top .gridline b overlapping by 19.2 x 8.0px at every one of them (1440: bar-val 1204.1-1272.4 x 375.0-389.8, gridline '12' 1245.8-1265.0 x 381.8-396.7). The overhang past .plot's right edge is 7.4px at 1440 and 1280, 12.4px at 768, 23.2px at 390, and at 390 .page's computed padding-right is 24px so the content edge is 366 and bar-val reaches 372.2 — 6.2px past it, exactly as claimed. .gridline b paints before .cols in DOM order with both at z-index auto, so its opaque paper background cannot mask the bar value: both numerals really are superimposed. It is REFUTED on the FIX, which is a no-op against the very defect it is written for. First, `.gridline:last-of-type` matches ZERO elements: .plot's span children are gridline, gridline, baseline, record, cols, so the last span OF TYPE is .cols, not a gridline — :last-of-type keys on tag, not class. Second, I applied the seat's stylesheet verbatim and re-measured: the overprint is byte-identical at 19.2 x 8.0 at both 1440 and 390. Right-aligning .bar-val to the last .colw only pulls its right edge from 1272.4 to 1265.0 — flush with the plot, which does fix the overhang — while the axis label 1245.8-1265.0 is now entirely INSIDE the value label's box, so the illegibility the finding is about is untouched. Third, even with the selector corrected the -30px number is wrong: clearing 14.85px of line box needs the axis label's bottom at or above 375.0, i.e. top of about -36px, not -30px (-30px still leaves ~5.7px of overlap). And -36px would strand the axis maximum three line-heights above the 100% rule it labels while the 50% label stays at -14px — two axis labels on two different offsets, which is a worse typographic result than the collision. The severity class 'defect' is correct and I am not correcting it: nothing untrue is asserted and the surface still works, but the live week's value is genuinely unreadable.
sharpenedFix: Do not dodge vertically — the right edge is oversubscribed (axis max, best-week tag, live value) and the answer is to reserve it. Give the plot a right gutter that only the columns are inset from, so the label rail is unoccupied: add `--gutter: 30px` on `.chart`, `.plot .cols { right: var(--gutter); }` and `.xaxis { padding-right: var(--gutter); }`, then right-align the live value with `.colw:last-child .bar-val { left: auto; right: 0; transform: none; }`. I measured this exact stylesheet at all four viewports: the axis label and the bar value separate by 10.8px of clear space at every one (1440: bar-val ends 1235.0, gridline '12' starts 1245.8), bar-val no longer crosses .plot's edge or the page margin at 390, bar and tick centres stay locked at 1440/1280/768, and bars keep their 22px cap. If the `record-tag-never-paints` gutter lands too, use ONE shared --gutter rather than two, and size it to the widest of the three labels ('Best week · 8' measures 102.7px, so the tag must keep right:0 on .record and sit in the gutter, not be inset by it). Leave `.gridline b { top: -14px }` alone — with the gutter it is already clear.
breaks: At 390 the x-axis already overflows before any change (.xaxis scrollWidth 317 vs width 308, because twelve `flex:1 1 0` ticks floor at their content width), so ticks are already ~9px out of register with bars at the right end; adding padding-right on top widens that to ~37px at the last tick. Re-measure bar-centre vs tick-centre at 390 and 430 after landing, and either drop --gutter to ~20px under a 430px query or fix the pre-existing overflow (the muted ticks are opacity:0, not display:none, so they still claim width). Also re-measure: the live bar loses ~2.5px of width at 390 (19.5px, already under the 22px cap) — check the hatched partial column still reads as hatched at that width; the .record dashed rule and .record-tag are NOT inset by the gutter, so confirm the tag still lands over paper and not over the axis rail; the first-run state has a single .colw and no gridlines, so `.colw:last-child` still matches there — confirm its lone bar-val does not now hug a gutter that has no labels in it; and re-run audit.mjs (the axis label keeps its --ink-3 on --paper contrast, but the gutter changes the composited backdrop behind .bar-val's accent) plus interaction-check.mjs.
